newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H sees earnings improvement in 1997.
newsitem.headline: W&H sees earnings improvement in 1997.

text.p: Publisher Wilson and Horton on Thursday reported a profit of NZ$40.12 million for the year to December 31 and said it was well positioned for further improvement in 1997.
Wilson and Horton also said the operating earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of the New Zealand Herald, New Zealand's largest-circulation newspaper, increased by 18 percent for the year.

Wilson and Horton, 85.37 percent owned by Irish publisher Independent Newspapers Plc, said the redesigned Herald, which was launched in late August, had resulted in a pleasing increase in circulation.
"However, all sectors slowed in the post-(October 12, 1996) election period prior to the formation of a government," Wilson and Horton said in a statement.
"Weaker retail advertising was partly compensated for by strong growth in national advertising."
The altered sections of the newspaper and the added use of colour were given editorial support at the expense initially of advertising ratios.

"These costs were considered essential to give the New Zealand Herald the opportunity to develop its new style. Increased advertising demand over recent weeks has restored former ratios with a consequent improvement in the paper's profitability," Wilson and Horton said.
W&H's regional and community papers were similarly affected by the slowdown in retail advertising, compounded by the strong New Zealand dollar which continued to hider rural markets.

"The magazine publishing division showed a decline in advertising volumes. Consequently the commercial printing division suffered reduced revenues from decreased pagination from both the company's own publications and those printed under contract and a lower demand for direct mail advertising material," W&H said.
It said the educational publishing group had a good year, with strong export growth in North America.

The Radio Network of New Zealand (formerly Radio New Zealand), in which W&H invested in July last year, had purchased Prospect Radio Group in September. Prospect is an Auckland and Hamilton-based group of stations which include the other major radio news service, IRN.

"Our joint venture partners, Australia Provincial Newspapers and Clear Channel Communications of the U.S.A., both have considerable experience in broadcasting. Technological investment has begun and this will be the basis for strong profit growth over the next few years," W&H said.

Currently the Radio Network owned 56 FM and AM stations with a wide coverage throughout New Zealand. Some frequencies would be disposed of during the next 12 months to meet Commerce Commission requirements following the purchase of Prospect Radio.
"The company is confident that having in excess of 60 percent of the advertising market, and with its strong network brands, growth in profitability will result," W&H said.
Independent Newspapers Plc's greater ownership in W&H was a positive move for the company as it provided opportunities through being part of a global group.
"Wilson and Horton is well positioned for further improvement in 1997," W&H said.
